title: An actor's own fields — software-analysis capability
description: One entry of the actors' collection file, `use-case-model/actors.md` under the analysis location (software-analysis DEC-001 points 1 to 3): a named role that uses the system, and the needs it brings. The entry is keyed by the actor's id (`analysis.schema.json#/$defs/actor-id`), which sits outside this object; its body section is the one headed by that id. These are the entry's own fields: its friction block sits in the methodology's container beside them and is the core's, validated by the backbone (COR-050, COR-053 point 10). An actor anchors to where the software or a decision embodies it (DEC-001 point 4); one nothing embodies carries the reason it has none as `unanchored-because` in its friction block, the core's key, never among these fields (DEC-001 point 9; COR-050 point 1). Applied by the capability's check, `pkit software-analysis validate` (the `software-analysis:artefacts` member of `pkit validate`); unknown fields are refused, so a misspelt one is never silently ignored.

name.description: The actor's display name. It may change; the id does not.

needs.description: What the actor needs from the system, one line each. A user story — a need in one sentence — is an actor's need and a use case's goal, not an artefact of its own (DEC-001 point 1).
